questions.question: What is the main advantage of BufferedWriter over writing directly with FileWriter?
options: BufferedWriter can write binary data
BufferedWriter is more efficient thanks to an internal buffer that reduces writes to disk
BufferedWriter allows writing to multiple files at once
BufferedWriter supports UTF-8 encoding and FileWriter does not
explanations: BufferedWriter works with text, not binary.
Correct. BufferedWriter accumulates data in an in-memory buffer and writes it to disk in blocks, significantly reducing I/O operations.
BufferedWriter only writes to one file at a time.
Both classes support UTF-8 through the appropriate encoding.

questions.question: What is the correct pattern for copying a text file in Java?
options: File.copy(source, destination)
Read with BufferedReader and write with BufferedWriter line by line
Files.copy() is the only possible way
new FileWriter(destination).write(new FileReader(source))
explanations: File does not have a static copy() method.
Correct. The classic pattern is to read each line with BufferedReader and write it with BufferedWriter for an efficient copy.
Files.copy() is an NIO alternative, but it is not the only way.
You cannot pass a FileReader directly to the write() method of FileWriter.

questions.question: What is PrintWriter in Java?
options: A class for printing to the console only
A Writer with formatting methods such as println() and printf()
A formatted file reader
A tool for generating PDF files
explanations: PrintWriter is not limited to the console; it can write to files.
Correct. PrintWriter extends Writer and offers convenient methods such as println() and printf() for writing formatted text.
PrintWriter writes, it does not read files.
PrintWriter does not generate PDF files.

questions.question: What is the difference between pw.write() and pw.println()?
options: write() writes binary and println() writes text
write() writes without a line break and println() adds a line break automatically
There is no difference, they are interchangeable
write() only accepts Strings and println() only accepts numbers
explanations: Both methods work with text.
Correct. write() writes the text as is without adding anything extra, while println() adds a line break after the content.
They are different in their behavior regarding line breaks.
Both methods accept several data types.

questions.question: When is it preferable to use Files.writeString() over FileWriter?
options: When you need to write character by character
When you already have the entire content and want to write it in a single operation
When you need to use try-with-resources
Files.writeString() only works for small files
explanations: Files.writeString() is not designed for character-by-character writing.
Correct. Files.writeString() is ideal when you already have the full content as a String and want to write it in a simple and concise way.
Both can be used with try-with-resources.
Files.writeString() has no size restriction.
